CENTRAL PROVINCE PROVINCIAL COUNCIL
The Order passed by the 24(2), (1), (xii), (xiii) clauses & 24(3) of the 1992 No. 04 Central Province
Road Passenger Carriage Service Statute passed as per the powers vested to the ProvincialCouncils by the 8th Sub document of the 13th amendment to the Constitution of the Democratic
Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka and the 20th clause of the year 2000 No. 01 Central Province
passenger Transport Services Authority Statute

I, Ediriweera Weerawardena, Minister of Road Development, transport, Power and Energy, Housing and Construction ofthe Central Provicial Council hereby announce under the powers vested in me by 24(2) (1), (xii), (xiii) clauses of the1992 No. 04 of the Central Province Road Passenger Carriage Service Statute and 20th clause of the year 2000 No. 01Central Province Passenger Transport Services Authority Statute shall revoke the orders made by the ExtraordinaryGazette No. 1990/48 of the Democratic Socialist Rupublic of Sri Lanka on 29.10.2016 and will pass the below mentionedorders in addition to the orders made on the new transport system named as "Sahasara" introduced by the Central ProvincePassenger Trasnsport Services Authority published by an Extraordinary Gazette No. 1990/27 of the Democratic SocialistRepublic of Sri Lanka on 27.10.2016 and with effect from the date of publication of the Gazette.
1.(i) The Central Province Passenger Transport Services Authority should Identify transport units through
one route or group of routes and announce them within 36 months from the date of the Minister'sorder ;
(ii) A manager should be appointed to administrate the announced route units according to the new system ;
(iii) A control unit should be established for each and every announced route unit or a group of routes.
2.(i) Route permit holders should provide passenger transport services in their route or routes within the date

of the route units announced or time period specified by the Passenger Transport Authority under theadministration of the manager appointed according to (1) ii by the Passenger Transport Services Authorityand new buses should operate within the approved route or a group of routes according to time tables,regulations and service standards given by the manager under the supervision of the authority.

(ii) All income earned on passenger and goods transport through electronic ticket machines and income

earned without an electronic machine due to a technical failure and all other income earned should bydeposited in a bank approved by the central province passenger transport services authority which isaccepted by the Central Bank in an account named "Central Province Passenger Transport ServicesAuthority."
(iii) Only the buses that comprise Central Province Passenger Transport Services Authority approved electronic
ticket machines with GPS, CCTV and GPRS technology should be given permission to passengertransportation.
(iv) Except in a case of a technical failure the passenger transportation charges should always be collected
through electronic cards.
(v) A complete control unit should be opended and maintained to obtain data and information from electronic
devices fixed on buses and the data should be captured, safe guarded and used for the efficiency of thebus service.
(vi) The Central Province Passenger Transport Service Authority should announce the amount of money that

will be paid for one kilo meter to owners of each route or group of routes based on the minimum distanceof the route or group of routes, the profit of each route and by the quality of the service provided bythem from time to time.
(vii) Bus owners who are forwarding documents to prove that they are contributing properly for employees
through Employee Provident Fund and Employee Trust Fund should be given the permission for passengertransports.
(viii) Only buses proven that they are operated properly in a route or a group of routes for 02 months after fixing
electronic devices should be included in the "Sahasara" operation system.
(ix) Bus reservations should be branded as "Sahasara".
(x) Management of the Bus Control Unit should be carried out by the Passenger transport services authority
or a bus service Manager approved by the Authority.
(xi) The Passenger transport services authrity should appoint investigation groups and transfer them the
required authority to investigate the efficiency of the transport services and proper bus transactions.
(xii) A suitable unit under the authority should be established to carry out and efficient public complaint
management.
(xiii) Suitable incentives should by provided to promote using electronic payment cards.
3. The Orders cited in 1 and 2 should immediately be implemented within all the routes of the central provincesoon after from the date of the publication of the Gazette notification.
4. The Passenger Transport Services Authority owns full authority of maintaining service quality & passengercomfort and all decisions taken to introduce new services.

5.(i) Passenger Transport Services Authority should carry out a route unit audit for technical and financial
audits by appointing qualified audit officers.
(ii) Should provide facilities to bus permit owners to check these audit reports when required.
(iii) These annual audit reports should by forwarded to the Provincial Council Through subject Minister.
EDIRIWEERA WEERAWARDENA,Minister of Road Development, Transport, Power and
